classification: CURRENT_FACT for every current_purpose / current_owner entry, verified by reading the 112 migrations, the 62 models, the seeders and the services. RECOMMENDATION for every verdict, creative_use, required_change and risk entry. OPEN_DECISION where noted.
status: PROPOSAL ONLY. No migration was written. No table was created, altered or dropped. This artifact exists to stop the Creative implementation from duplicating infrastructure that already exists.
purpose: The table-level reuse decision record required by section 11 of the Creative Marketplace audit. It answers, for every one of the 73 tables in the current database: what is it for, who owns it, what Creative would use it for, whether Creative should reuse / extend / pattern after / avoid it, why, what change would be required, and what the risk is.
method: Read all 112 migrations in database/migrations to establish the real table set, columns, keys and constraints.
Read all 62 Eloquent models to establish ownership and relationships.
Read the seeders to establish which role and permission values actually exist.
Cross-checked against 08-creative-database-current-schema-map.json; every verdict here is at least as strict as the verdict recorded there.
Group index: the Creative blueprint is in 09-creative-database-target-schema-blueprint.json. This artifact covers only what already exists.

classification_legend.CURRENT_FACT: Verified from source code (migrations, models, seeders, services).
classification_legend.ARCHITECTURE_DOCUMENT: Defined by docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE_RULES.md or root AGENTS.md.
classification_legend.INFERENCE: Reasonably inferred from the implementation or from relationships between tables.
classification_legend.RECOMMENDATION: Recommended target design. Not implemented. No migration was written.
classification_legend.OPEN_DECISION: Cannot be determined from available evidence; requires a product or architecture decision.

verdict_legend.DIRECT_REUSE: Creative reads/writes this table with no schema change.
verdict_legend.EXTEND: Creative reuses the table but must add rows (role, permission, setting group, recipient type). Adding COLUMNS to shared tables is only proposed where explicitly stated.
verdict_legend.EXTEND_BY_REFERENCE: Creative must reference this table from a new Creative table. No column is added to the shared table.
verdict_legend.PATTERN_ONLY: Creative must build its own table. The existing table is read only as a structural/idiomatic template.
verdict_legend.DO_NOT_USE: Creative must neither read nor write this table, and must not extend it.

baseline.foreign_key_definitions_note: 94 via ->constrained(...) plus 2 legacy ->foreign(...) across the 112 migrations. The earlier figure of 91 in this artifact was an undercount; the AGENTS.md figure of 94 is the ->constrained() count alone. Three FK-like columns are NOT constrained: bookings.screen_category_id, booking_screens.screen_category_id, booking_screens.screen_provider_id, asset_coverage_cities.state_id (4 columns).
baseline.statement: Every table below is a pre-existing Project 01 table. None of them is a Creative table.

how_to_read.DIRECT_REUSE: Safe to depend on directly. No Creative schema work.
how_to_read.EXTEND: Creative adds ROWS to an existing shared table (a role, a permission, a setting group, a recipient type). Adding COLUMNS to a shared table is never proposed here except where the required_change text says so explicitly - and it does not.
how_to_read.EXTEND_BY_REFERENCE: A new Creative table references the existing table by FK. The existing table is unchanged.
how_to_read.PATTERN_ONLY: Creative builds its own table. The existing table is read as a structural template only. This is the most common verdict for the advertising and financial tables, and it is deliberate: the SHAPE is reusable, the TABLE is not.
how_to_read.DO_NOT_USE: Creative must not read, write or extend the table. Most of these are marketing content or advertising inventory.

creative_use.statement: Add one 'creator' role row. Possibly one 'reviewer' role row if Creative review is separated from administration.

verdict.meaning: Creative reuses the table but must add rows (role, permission, setting group, recipient type). Adding COLUMNS to shared tables is only proposed where explicitly stated.

reuse_matrix.why: RolePermissionChecker resolves permissions by role slug only, so Creative permissions cannot work without a role row.
reuse_matrix.required_change: INSERT a role row (slug 'creator'). No schema change; roles already has unique name and unique slug. CRITICAL COUPLING, verified 2026-09-26: RolePermissionChecker::permissionsForRole() resolves a SINGLE slug from the users.role column, so one user holds exactly one role. Setting users.role='creator' to grant creative.* permissions REMOVES every other permission that user had. For a user who is both advertiser and creator, a 'creator' role row alone is therefore insufficient and actively destructive. OD-DB-08 / OD-AUTH-01 is BLOCKING and must be answered before any role row is added. Options: (a) also grant creative.* to the existing buyer role, (b) derive creator capability from the existence of a creators row and keep creator permissions out of role_permissions, or (c) a role-join model, which is a platform authorization change requiring its own authorisation. Do not choose silently.

risk.statement: Adding a role is additive. The risk is not the insert but the temptation to add a second permission-resolution path.

tables_creative_must_not_duplicate.statement: The following infrastructure already exists. Creating a second instance of any of it during Creative implementation is a duplicate-infrastructure defect, not a design choice.

items.do_not_create: a creative_roles / creative_permissions / creative authorization resolver
items.instead: add a creator role row and creative.* permission rows (both blocked by OD-DB-08 until the single-slug role model is resolved)

items.do_not_create: a creative currency or FX table or a second rate fetch
items.instead: read currency_rates through the existing exchange-rate infrastructure

items.do_not_create: a creative payment gateway interface or a second Razorpay client
items.instead: reuse the existing gateway contract; only the payment RECORD is Creative-specific

items.do_not_create: a creative storage disk, a creative upload pipeline or a second image processor
items.instead: reuse the disks and the image-processing contract; Creative needs a file RECORD and an ACCESS RULE, not new infrastructure

items.do_not_create: creative_activity_logs or a per-entity Creative timeline table
a creative notification log or a second mail dispatch path
items.instead: extend recipient_type and add Creative Mailables

items.do_not_create: a Creative cache, queue, lock or session store

items.instead: add a creative group of key/value settings (financial rules excluded)

tables_creative_must_extend.statement: Only six existing tables receive Creative additions, and every addition is rows, not columns. Two of the six (roles, role_permissions) are blocked by OD-DB-08 - see blocking_caveat.

items.addition: one 'creator' role row - CONDITIONAL on OD-DB-08; see blocking_caveat
creative.* permission grants - CONDITIONAL on OD-DB-08; see blocking_caveat

tables_creative_must_extend.blocking_caveat: RolePermissionChecker::permissionsForRole() resolves a SINGLE slug from the users.role column, so one user holds exactly one role. Setting users.role='creator' strips every other permission that user had, so a 'creator' role row alone is insufficient - and actively destructive - for a user who is both advertiser and creator. OD-DB-08 / OD-AUTH-01 is BLOCKING and must be answered before any of the roles or role_permissions rows below are inserted.

highest_risk_reuse_decisions.risk: A Creative project written into bookings would change advertising pricing, availability, settlement, revenue splits and 20+ routes. This is the single highest-consequence misuse available in this schema.
highest_risk_reuse_decisions.control: creative_projects is a separate table with no FK to bookings; any future 'attach a creative project to a campaign' feature must be an explicit, separately authorised cross-domain decision.

highest_risk_reuse_decisions.risk: Reusing the public marketing rating surface for commercial Creative reviews would place review data with no author binding, no ownership, no soft delete and public edit paths.
highest_risk_reuse_decisions.control: Creative reviews are a new table bound to project + author + state.

highest_risk_reuse_decisions.risk: Relaxing payments.booking_id (NOT NULL, CASCADE) to accommodate Creative funding would alter an existing financial table and every booking payment query.
highest_risk_reuse_decisions.control: creative_fundings references the gateway contract, not the payments table.

highest_risk_reuse_decisions.risk: Copying its file columns without adding visibility, ownership and an access check reproduces a file-access gap for client and creator files.
highest_risk_reuse_decisions.control: Creative file records carry owner, visibility and an authorization check at read time.

highest_risk_reuse_decisions.risk: Terminology collision: 'Asset' in this repository means advertising inventory. A developer looking for Creative assets will find screens and booking_media first.
highest_risk_reuse_decisions.control: Creative names its own aggregate 'CreativeFile' and never uses the word Asset for it.

highest_risk_reuse_decisions.risk: Copying the commission columns without the lockForUpdate discipline of PartnerCommissionRepositoryInterface::findOrFailForUpdate would allow double payment under concurrency.
highest_risk_reuse_decisions.control: The Creative earnings service applies the same pessimistic lock before any state change.

highest_risk_reuse_decisions.risk: Integer points representation leaking into a money ledger would introduce a precision defect into a financial record.
highest_risk_reuse_decisions.control: Creative money is decimal(12,2) plus an explicit currency column.

new_tables_required_summary.statement: Creative requires new tables because NO existing table can hold its aggregates. The authoritative design is in 09-creative-database-target-schema-blueprint.json; this artifact only records why reuse is not sufficient.
new_tables_required_summary.reason: No existing table has (a) a creator identity, (b) a purchasable creative service with a rate, (c) a brief, (d) a proposal with a server-derived quote, (e) a project with revision and delivery lifecycle, (f) a client review bound to a transaction, or (g) a creator money ledger and payout period. The closest tables in the schema (partners, screen_providers, bookings, products) each fail on ownership semantics or on financial representation.
new_tables_required_summary.count_note: The exact table count, names, columns, indexes and the migration order are in artifact 09. They are not duplicated here, and no migration exists.

open_decisions.question: Can one user be both an advertiser and a creator?
open_decisions.impact_on_schema: If yes, Creative must NOT express the creator role in users.role; it must be derived from the existence of a creative_creators row.
open_decisions.missing_information: Product decision. No source evidence either way. The current users.role free-text column cannot express a dual role.

open_decisions.question: Is Creative single-currency (INR) at launch?
open_decisions.impact_on_schema: Determines whether every Creative money table needs a currency column and whether currency_rates is read at all.
open_decisions.missing_information: Product decision. Note that the existing screen_provider_settlements table has NO currency column, so copying its shape would silently assume single currency.

open_decisions.question: Does Creative need a commission percentage, and is it per service, per category, or global?
open_decisions.impact_on_schema: If yes it needs a versioned Creative commission table so historical earnings stay reproducible. It must NOT live in settings.
open_decisions.missing_information: Product decision on the commercial model. The existing illuvision_percentage / screen_provider_percentage defaults are provider-specific and must not be inherited.

open_decisions.question: Are creator KYC / payout details stored in this database?
open_decisions.impact_on_schema: If yes, a Creative payout-details record with its own retention and access rules is required. It must not be added to users.
open_decisions.missing_information: Product and compliance decision. No existing KYC table exists in the schema (password_setup_tokens is an invitation token, not KYC).

open_decisions.question: Does Creative reuse the activity_logs table for its audit trail?
open_decisions.impact_on_schema: Determines whether a Creative-scoped audit table is needed.
open_decisions.missing_information: Confirmation that activity_logs can express a Creative subject polymorphically. Flagged for verification before the audit-trail phase.

open_decisions.question: Are Creative briefs targeted to a chosen creator/service or posted as an open opportunity?
open_decisions.impact_on_schema: Determines whether a junction table and a proposal-uniqueness constraint are required.
open_decisions.missing_information: Product decision. It also determines whether 'one open proposal per creator' can be a database constraint or only an application rule.

open_decisions.question: Are Creative files private by default and delivered by signed URL, or public?
open_decisions.impact_on_schema: Determines the visibility column semantics on the Creative file record and whether the existing public disk may be used at all.
open_decisions.missing_information: Security decision. The current platform has no signed-URL mechanism, so 'private' is new work regardless of the answer.
